issues.failure_explanation: The Green condition \eqref{SRCd} is stated one-sided, without absolute value. Any solution with $u(r\xi)\le a\log r+O(1/r)$ satisfies it by choosing $b>a$; in particular, for $R\neq1$ and $g=0$ the functions $u=c\,\log(r/R)$ ($c>0$) solve the homogeneous exterior Laplace problem and satisfy \eqref{SRCd}, so uniqueness fails. Hence Proposition PropProblems.2b (well-posedness, i.e. unique continuous solvability with operator $\mathrm{S}^{\log}$) is false as stated, and the operators $\mathrm{S}^{\log}$, $\DtNlog$ are not well defined. The uniqueness cited from McLean [Thm 8.16] uses the two-sided logarithmic decay condition; the written premise is strictly weaker.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Insert the absolute value in \eqref{SRCd}, i.e. require $|u(r\xi)-b\log r|\le Cr^{-1}$ (as in the parallel condition for $\operatorname{IC}_s^{\operatorname{strong}}$ and in $\operatorname{IC}_0^{\operatorname{isom}}$); uniqueness via \cite[Thm 8.16]{Mclean00} and all subsequent uses are then restored unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: Proposition PropProblems.2b is false as written; the definition of $\mathrm{S}^{\log}$/$\DtNlog$ (Section 2.2), the characterization of $\operatorname{IC}_0^{\operatorname{Green}}$ by $\partial_r u=\DtNlog(u|_{S_R})$, and Lemma lem:two dimensions (which compares $\DtNLaplace$ and $\DtNlog$) lose their foundation.
issues.title: One-sided Green condition at infinity (n=2, s=0) destroys uniqueness of the exterior problem
issues.why_classification: A one-symbol strengthening of the condition to two-sided decay is a local, routine repair; the proposition, the $\mathrm{S}^{\log}$/$\DtNlog$ operators and Lemma lem:two dimensions then hold exactly as advertised, with no loss of content.

issues.title: Fourier-coefficient estimates in the proof of well-posedness of the exterior Laplace problem are false
issues.why_classification: The repair is a contained recomputation of routine integral estimates plus a weight adjustment and separate handling of the mean mode; no new proof architecture is needed and every substantive claim of the proposition survives, but several interdependent displays must be reworked, which exceeds a short local fix.

issues.failure_explanation: By \eqref{eqn:DtN_def} the pairing on $S_R$ is $\langle\operatorname{DtN}(s)g,\bar g\rangle_{S_R}=R^{n-2}\sum_m z_{m,\nu}(sR)|\hat g_{m,j}|^2$. For $s=0$ and the constant mode $z^\Delta_{0,\nu}=-(n-2)$, so $-\operatorname{Re}\langle\operatorname{DtN}(0)c,\bar c\rangle=\frac{n-2}{R}\|g\|^2_{L^2(S_R)}$. The claimed lower bound $\frac{n-2}{2}\|g\|^2$ (with no $R$-dependent constant, since only the upper bound carries $C(n)$) fails whenever $R>2$: for $n=3$, $R=3$, $g\equiv1$, $-\operatorname{Re}\langle\operatorname{DtN}(0)g,\bar g\rangle=\tfrac13\|g\|^2<\tfrac12\|g\|^2$. The proof only treats $R=1$ and invokes scaling, which yields $\frac{n-2}{2R}$, a strictly weaker conclusion than stated.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Insert the scaling factor, i.e. state $\frac{n-2}{2R}\|g\|^2_{L^2(S_R)}\le-\operatorname{Re}\langle\operatorname{DtN}(s)g,\bar g\rangle_{S_R}$; this is exactly what the unit-sphere proof gives after scaling and every application in the paper remains valid.
issues.overall_effect: The coercivity statement of Theorem thm:DtN(iii) is false as written for $R>2$; the theorem as stated is invalid. Its uses (e.g. in the proof of Theorem thm:C_Friedrich) rely only on the vanishing consequence $\operatorname{DtN}(s)u=0\Rightarrow u|_{S_R}=0$, which survives the corrected constant.
issues.title: Lower bound in Theorem thm:DtN(iii) is false for large radii (missing factor 1/R)
issues.why_classification: A one-token correction to the statement; the corrected bound is the natural scaling of what is actually proved, and no downstream result uses the $R$-independence of the constant, so there is no mathematical loss.

issues.failure_explanation: By \eqref{eqn:Im_w0} the spectral coefficient of the constant mode satisfies $-\operatorname{Im}z_{0,0}(s)\le c_2+|\operatorname{Im}s|$, which is not dominated by $C|\operatorname{Im}s|$: for $n=2$, $g\equiv1$ and $s=-ik\to0$, $-\operatorname{Im}z_{0,0}(-ik)=\operatorname{Im}w_0(k)=\frac{2}{\pi M_0^2(k)}\sim\frac{\pi/2}{\log^2(1/k)}$ while $|\operatorname{Im}s|=k\to0$, so the ratio tends to infinity. The displayed inequality $\mp\operatorname{Im}\langle\operatorname{DtN}(s)g,\bar g\rangle\le C(n)|\operatorname{Im}s|\|g\|^2_{L^2(S_1)}$ is therefore false, and the proof of Theorem thm:DtN(iv) is broken at this step.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Keep the mode-wise bounds from Theorem thm:zmn.iii, i.e. $\mp\operatorname{Im}\langle\operatorname{DtN}(s)g,\bar g\rangle\le(c_2+|\operatorname{Im}s|)\|g\|^2_{L^2(S_1)}$, and conclude $\le\max(c_2,1)(\|g\|^2_{H^{1/2}(S_1)}+|s|\|g\|^2_{L^2(S_1)})\le C(n)\|g\|^2_{H^{1/2}(S_1),s}$, which is exactly the claimed item (iv).
issues.overall_effect: The proof of Theorem thm:DtN does not establish item (iv); the statement of (iv) itself is nevertheless true and is recovered with the corrected estimate.
issues.title: False intermediate bound in the proof of Theorem thm:DtN(iv) (constant term dropped)
issues.why_classification: A local correction of one displayed estimate, using the constant $c_2$ already established in Theorem thm:zmn.iii, preserves the theorem's statement verbatim; no argument or construction must be redesigned.

issues.failure_explanation: Two independent gaps invalidate the contradiction argument. (i) The negation of \eqref{eqn:C_F} produces sequences with $\|\nabla v_k\|^2+\|\partial_r v_k\|^2_{H^{-1/2}(S_R)}\to0$; the proof instead assumes $\|\partial_r v_k\|_{L^2(S_R)}\to0$, a strictly stronger smallness (the $L^2$ norm of $\partial_r v_k$ need not even be finite), so the case actually to be excluded is never treated. (ii) $H$ is defined as a union over $z\in\mathbb{C}_{\ge0}$ of kernels; that it is a Hilbert space (a linear closed subspace) is asserted via 'completeness follows from the continuity of DtN(s)', which does not follow, and consequently the claim that the weak limit $u$ belongs to $H$ — on which the final step '$\operatorname{DtN}(s)u=0$ and thm:DtN.iii imply $\frac{n-2}{2}\|u\|^2_{L^2(S_R)}=0$' rests — is unsupported. The proof therefore does not establish \eqref{eqn:C_F} as stated.

failure_location.quote:
Since this sequence is bounded in $H$, it admits a weakly convergent
subsequence with weak limit $u\in H$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Keep the compactness setup but drop the appeal to completeness of $H$: each $v_k$ satisfies $\gamma_1 v_k=\operatorname{DtN}(z_k)(\gamma_0 v_k)$ with its own $z_k$; test against $\overline{\gamma_0 v_k}$, use $\|\gamma_1 v_k\|_{H^{-1/2}}\to0$ and boundedness of $\gamma_0 v_k$ in $H^{1/2}$ to get $\langle\operatorname{DtN}(z_k)g_k,\bar g_k\rangle\to0$, and apply Theorem thm:DtN(iii) mode-wise to conclude $\|\gamma_0 u\|_{L^2(S_R)}\to0$, contradicting $\|u\|_{L^2(\Omega)}=1$ for $n\ge3$; also state the contradiction hypothesis with the $H^{-1/2}$ norm. No completeness of the union space is needed.
issues.overall_effect: Theorem thm:C_Friedrich is not proved; the wavenumber-independent Friedrichs inequality and, through it, Corollary CorTrace (estimates \eqref{eqn:C_F_s} and \eqref{esttr} and the displayed small-wavenumber inequality) are left unsupported.
issues.title: Compactness proof of the Friedrichs-type inequality is incomplete (wrong norm; unsupported membership of the limit)
issues.why_classification: The theorem's statement survives, but the repair requires replacing the final step of the proof by a different, though standard and contained, compactness argument (weak convergence plus compact trace convergence plus Theorem thm:DtN.iii); this is more than a local fix and is not a mere omitted algebra step.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
Consider a bounded
Lipschitz domain $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^{n}$ in $n\geq3$ dimensions such
that $S_{R}\subset\partial\Omega$ is relatively closed in $\partial\Omega$.

\left.  \left(  -\Delta v+s^{2}v\right)  \right\vert _{\omega}=0 & \text{for
some }\omega\subset\Omega\text{ such that }S_{R}\text{ is a relatively closed
subset of }\partial\omega,

issues.failure_explanation: The corollary assumes only $(-\Delta v+s^2v)|_\omega=0$ for some $\omega\subset\Omega$ with $S_R\subset\partial\omega$ relatively closed, which permits $\omega$ with $S_R$ lying in the interior of $\Omega$ (e.g. $\Omega=B_2$, $\omega=B_R$). The proof, however, invokes Theorem thm:C_Friedrich on the domain $\Omega$, whose hypothesis is that $S_R\subset\partial\Omega$ is relatively closed in $\partial\Omega$ — a hypothesis the corollary never states and that the stated assumptions do not imply. The invocation is therefore outside the theorem's hypotheses, and neither \eqref{eqn:C_F_s}, \eqref{esttr} nor the displayed 'in particular' estimate is established for the stated class of $v$.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypothesis that $S_R\subset\partial\Omega$ is relatively closed (as in Theorem thm:C_Friedrich), which is what the intended applications provide; the proof then applies verbatim. Alternatively, re-derive \eqref{eqn:C_F_s} by running the compactness argument on $\Omega$ with the $S_R$-normal trace controlled through $\omega$ via \eqref{normaltraceest}.
issues.overall_effect: The conclusions \eqref{eqn:C_F_s} and \eqref{esttr} and the final displayed inequality of Corollary CorTrace are unproved as stated; the constants $C_{\operatorname{tr}}$ and the $C_{\operatorname{F}}$-dependence are not justified under the stated hypotheses.
issues.title: Proof of the trace corollary applies the Friedrichs theorem outside its hypotheses
issues.why_classification: Adding one standard hypothesis (already satisfied in the intended truncated-domain setting) makes the proof valid verbatim; all conclusions, constants and advertised scope survive without any new argument.
